title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using generative AI to create deepfakes of voices and images to impersonate specific trusted individuals, including a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to target immigrants seeking legal services. The scams operate at scale, with Americans reporting nearly $893 million in AI-enabled fraud losses in a single year. This is impersonation enabled by a technology deployed without authentication checks by the scammers themselves, who access public material from social media to build convincing fakes.

The failure occurs in the interaction between victim and scammer, where no verification mechanism exists to confirm identity before money changes hands. A victim attempting to hire an immigration attorney or seeking emergency help has no reliable way to distinguish a deepfaked voice or image from the real person, especially when the scammer has researched personal details to increase credibility. It would have taken either a pre-established verification protocol, such as a code word known only to family members, or institutional checks such as financial transfers routed through verified channels rather than direct wire transfers to confirm identity before loss occurs.

It is not established whether any particular AI platform intentionally enabled these scams or whether the tools were misused against the platforms' terms of service.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to commit scams by creating deepfakes of voices, photos, and phone calls to impersonate trusted individuals and steal money. Recent cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to target immigrants and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses last year, with Florida reporting 350 complaints totaling $39.9 million and Georgia reporting 71 complaints totaling $10.4 million in losses.

Scammers use generative AI to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photographs, and research personal relationships to make schemes more convincing. Common AI scams include grandparent scams, romance schemes, and fake investment opportunities. The Georgia Attorney General's office recommends families establish code words to verify identity during emergencies, and financial institutions urge customers to verify requests through trusted channels rather than responding immediately to suspicious communications.
